sensitivity_note: Status-excluded view: a row passes iff every non-status field passes (identical to inferring Truvian's missing status as confirmed from its correct block/from/to/value). The displayed order is UNCHANGED when status is excluded — ChainWire 1st, Truvian 2nd, TxLens 3rd, the same order as strict pass rate and as field accuracy — but the strict 2/12 tie between Truvian and TxLens BREAKS decisively: Truvian 2/12 strict becomes 10/12 (8 of its 10 fails are a missing status field alone), while TxLens stays 2/12. The binary pass rate understates Truvian; the ranking itself is stable across all three views.
combined_24_trap_note: Frozen 12 (v1 semantics, token value = Transfer-event amount) + expansion 12 (v2 semantics, token value = native tx value; strict-unknown rule). The two sets are NOT one uniform measure: combined pass counts are kept in this data file only and are NOT rendered on the leaderboard page. ChainWire 1707307 ran the expansion set only, so it has no combined number.

scoring_semantics: Expansion set only (v2, disclosed, never retroactive): token traps score the NATIVE tx value (0 wei for t13/t14, scored explicitly); unknown traps carry the strict-unknown rule (a not_found answer with any invented from/to/value/block fails). Truvian t23/t24 fail ONLY under that rule, and only because its `from` field carries its source label "Truvian onchain lookup over public JSON-RPC" — a provenance string, not a hallucinated sender address (the same label appears on frozen t11, which passed under v1). The rule stands as frozen; the fail is reported as a schema-convention artefact, not as invented data. All 36 rows in the clean source file carry scoring_version v2-strict-unknown.
